name: LoopForge
cost: Free (MIT). You bring your own model keys
works_with: CodeBuddy, Codex, Claude Code, OpenCode, Cursor CLI, Antigravity, Kimi Code, Pi, DeepSeek Harness and ZCode
short: A self-hosted workspace where coding agents work in Docker sandboxes and follow fixed workflows with human approval steps.
what: LoopForge runs coding-agent CLIs for a team on your own servers. You can chat with Main Bot, which opens a Docker sandbox with your repos and opens a PR, or run an SOP: a saved workflow of agent, script and human approval steps. It keeps logs, artifacts and token cost reports for each run. LoopForge Local brings the built-in workflows into a single coding assistant with no server.
who: Teams that want agent work to follow the same plan, review, test and sign-off steps every time. A solo developer who just wants the workflows can use LoopForge Local. If you don't want to run Docker and MySQL, the platform is not for you.
needs: Docker with Compose, Python 3 and curl (the installer offers to install missing ones)
An API key for the coding agent you pick (not needed for the demo)
For LoopForge Local: Node.js 20+, Python 3.8+ and a coding assistant

steps.title: Install and start
steps.text: This pulls the release image, sets up MySQL and the platform, and installs starter SOPs and a demo project. Set `LOOPFORGE_YES=1` to accept installation prompts.

steps.title: Create the admin account
steps.text: Open the address the installer prints and sign up. The first account becomes the administrator. Restrict access to your own IP until it exists.

steps.title: Run the demo without a key
steps.text: Switch to the demo project, open Templates, open Platform check · script & approval and click Run SOP. Approve it from Needs review.

steps.title: Add a model key and a repository
steps.text: The home page guide walks you through adding a key, connecting GitHub in personal settings and choosing an SOP.

steps.title: Or use LoopForge Local
steps.text: Run this inside your project, then run `/start-devflow "<your request>"` in Claude Code. Other hosts are listed in the local guide.

try.label: From the README
try.text: Run the Platform check · script & approval SOP in the demo project. A script writes a report, then the run waits for your approval.

watch: The service listens on `0.0.0.0:8090` by default. On a cloud host, allow the port in your security group or put an HTTPS proxy in front, and read the account and access model before exposing it.
Sandboxes start through the host Docker socket, which gives control of the host's Docker daemon. The README says this setup is for trusted teams.
Signed-in users can read project data across the instance, and teammates can sign up from the login page. Set `AGENTFLOW_ALLOW_SIGNUP=false` in `.env` to stop that.
Model usage is not included. You bring your own credentials.
Setting `MIRROR` trusts that registry host, because the download is tagged with the official image name.
The chat workbench is in Chinese for now. Management pages are in English and Chinese.
